items.followUp: Two algorithms solve the same problem. What factors would you compare to choose the more efficient one? Give an example.

rubric.why: Time and memory use are key measures for comparing algorithm efficiency.
rubric.description: Compare the algorithms’ execution time and memory use.
rubric.how: Award for naming both time and memory use.

rubric.why: An algorithm must solve the problem correctly, not merely quickly.
rubric.description: Check that the algorithms produce the correct result.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning correctness or the correct result.

rubric.why: A specific example demonstrates how two algorithms for the same task can be compared.
rubric.description: Gives binary search and linear search as an example pair.
rubric.how: Award for naming both algorithms as alternatives for searching.

rubric.why: The input conditions affect which algorithm is suitable.
rubric.description: Explains that binary search needs sorted data, while linear search can be used on unsorted data.
rubric.how: Award for linking either search algorithm to the relevant input condition.

modelAnswer: Compare the algorithms’ execution time and memory use for the given input.
Check that each algorithm produces the correct result and meets the problem’s requirements.
For example, binary search takes less time than linear search on a large, sorted list.
Binary search requires sorted data, while linear search can be used on an unsorted list; choose the suitable algorithm for the input and resource requirements.

items.followUp: Give two ways encryption helps keep everyday internet use secure.

rubric.why: Explains the basic change encryption makes to information.
rubric.description: States that encryption changes readable information into coded information.
rubric.how: Award for identifying both the readable form and the coded form.

rubric.why: Identifies how encryption protects information from outsiders.
rubric.description: States that encryption helps prevent unauthorized people from reading data, including if it is intercepted.
rubric.how: Award for clearly describing protection from unauthorized reading.

rubric.why: Provides a relevant everyday internet use of encryption.
rubric.description: Gives an example such as online banking or online payments.
rubric.how: Award for one valid everyday example.

rubric.why: Identifies information that people commonly need to keep private online.
rubric.description: Mentions protection of personal information, passwords, or private messages.
rubric.how: Award for naming at least one relevant type of information.

modelAnswer: Encryption converts readable information (plaintext) into coded information (ciphertext).
It helps prevent unauthorized people from reading data, even if the data is intercepted.
It protects everyday online activities such as online banking and making payments.
It also helps keep personal information, passwords, and private messages private.

items.followUp: What is the use of a flow-line in a flowchart?

rubric.why: Identifies what a connector symbol links in a flowchart.
rubric.description: States that a connector joins separated parts or symbols of a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it connects parts or symbols.

rubric.why: Explains how the connector helps the reader follow a flowchart when its parts are separated.
rubric.description: States that it indicates where the flow continues, including onto another page.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that it marks the continuation of the flow.

modelAnswer: A connector symbol connects separated parts of a flowchart.
It shows where the flow continues, for example when the flowchart continues elsewhere on the page or on another page.

rubric.why: Identifies the text displayed by the HTML body.
rubric.description: Gives the displayed text, “I am student”.
rubric.how: Award for the exact displayed words, regardless of formatting.

rubric.why: Recognizes the formatting produced by the italic tag.
rubric.description: States that the displayed text is italicized.

modelAnswer: The browser displays: I am student.
The text is italic because it is enclosed in the <I> tag.

rubric.why: Identifies that non-volatile memory preserves its contents.
rubric.description: States that non-volatile memory retains its stored data.
rubric.how: Award for saying that it retains or keeps stored data.

rubric.why: Distinguishes non-volatile memory by its ability to retain data without power.
rubric.description: States that data remains when the power is switched off or removed.
rubric.how: Award for explicitly connecting data retention with loss of power.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory is memory that retains its stored data even when the power is switched off or removed.
